transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been feeling low for a long time. I still do my routes and my volunteer shifts, but most days there’s this heaviness—I’m just going through the motions, not really feeling like I’m in my own life.
How long have you been feeling this way—days, weeks, months, or longer?
About three years now—since my father died.

When you say you feel like you're not really in your own life, do you mean you feel emotionally flat and uninterested, or do you feel strangely detached or unreal, like you're watching yourself from outside?
It’s more that I feel low and heavy most days. I’m still doing what I need to do, but it feels like I’m just going through the motions, not really living my life.

Over these three years, has your mood stayed at about the same low level the whole time, or have there been certain weeks or months when things got much worse—like losing interest in almost everything, major changes in sleep or appetite, or trouble concentrating—compared to how you feel most of the time?

It’s mostly stayed at that same low level. I keep doing my routes and the volunteer work, but there’s this heaviness most days, like I’m just going through the motions instead of really being in my life.
Right now, are you also noticing changes in your sleep, appetite, energy, or ability to concentrate, or is it mainly just that low, heavy mood?

My sleep’s been off. Before a run, I’ll lie awake thinking through the next day’s stops, or I wake up around four and can’t really get back to sleep. I still get to work on time, but I start the day already worn down.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed a marked loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy—even your volunteer work or other activities?
I’m not sure I’d call it a marked loss. I still do the things I’m supposed to do, including the volunteer work. It just feels more like effort than enjoyment most of the time.
Besides the low mood and sleep changes, have you noticed feeling unusually fatigued or low on energy, or having thoughts that you're worthless or excessively guilty, over the past couple of weeks?

I do get down on myself. I keep comparing myself to the kind of man my dad was, and even though nobody’s saying I’m failing, I hear it in my own head. Like I should be further along and handling things better than I am.
Over the past two weeks, have you been feeling unusually fatigued or low on energy nearly every day?

Yeah, pretty much. I’m still showing up for work and the pantry, but everything takes more pushing than it used to. I’ve even left my logistics supervisor application unfinished because I don’t really trust myself to keep up with it.
During these past three years, has there ever been a stretch of two months or more where you felt essentially back to your normal self, without that heaviness or low mood?
No, I don’t think so. It’s been there pretty steadily for about three years now, ever since my father died.
Over the past two weeks, have you noticed any significant change in your appetite or weight, either increased or decreased?
I haven’t really noticed any big change in my appetite or weight.
Over the past two weeks, have you had trouble concentrating or making decisions, more than usual?
Yeah. I can still do my job, but lately I’ll reread delivery times or just stare at the schedule board longer than I should. My mind doesn’t seem to lock onto things the way it used to.
Over the past two weeks, have you had any thoughts of death or of hurting yourself, or feelings that you'd be better off not being here?
I’m not sure what you mean by thoughts of death. I’ve been feeling low, but I don’t really know how to answer that.
Would you say the sleep trouble, low energy, and trouble concentrating you've described are worse than usual right now, or have they felt about the same as they have for the past three years?
It’s been about the same, really. It started after my father died, about three years ago, and it’s just kind of stayed that way.

Would you say that right now these symptoms—the low mood, poor sleep, low energy, and trouble concentrating—are significantly interfering with your ability to do your job or maintain relationships, or are you managing to function close to your usual level despite them?

I’m still showing up for work and helping at the pantry, so I’m managing. But everything takes more pushing than it used to. I’ve got this application for a logistics supervisor position just sitting unfinished because I don’t really trust myself to keep up with it.

At any time in the past three years, has there been a stretch of two weeks or more when your mood and other symptoms became noticeably worse than your usual baseline—more intense sadness, lower energy, or worse concentration than what you've described as your ongoing pattern?
No, I don’t think there’s been a period where it got noticeably worse than this. It’s mostly just stayed at this same level.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient describes a chronic, low-grade depressive mood persisting steadily for approximately three years since his father's death, without ever meeting full criteria for a major depressive episode and without a two-month symptom-free interval. Associated features include poor sleep (early waking, pre-sleep rumination), low energy, diminished concentration, and self-critical thoughts, but no marked anhedonia, no appetite/weight change, and no suicidal ideation. Functioning is preserved though effortful (continues work and volunteering, though avoiding a promotion application). The chronicity (>2 years), lack of symptom-free periods, and subthreshold severity relative to major depression support persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia) rather than MDD, and the absence of episodic worsening or discrete onset/offset argues against an adjustment disorder despite the temporal link to bereavement.

confirmed_symptoms: Chronic low, heavy mood most days for ~3 years
Sleep disturbance: early morning waking, pre-sleep rumination
Difficulty concentrating (rereading schedules, staring at boards)
Self-critical thoughts/low self-esteem (comparing self unfavorably to father)
Feelings described as 'going through the motions' rather than true anhedonia
No distinct 2-week period of acute worsening beyond baseline
